headline: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weights coding model for local use
summary: This new AI model is optimized for always-on local agent workflows and can run on a PC or Mac with a single consumer GPU.
details: Meta Superintelligence Labs has introduced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter AI model. The model weights are being open-sourced under a permissive Apache 2.0 license, making it accessible for developers to build and run their own AI agents.

Muse Glimmer is designed for 'always-on local agent workflows,' meaning it can operate efficiently on personal computers or Macs equipped with a single consumer GPU. This local capability allows for AI use cases such as coding assistance, function calling, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, even without an internet connection.

To make the model viable on local hardware, Meta employed several optimization techniques. This includes a novel distillation process to transfer agentic reasoning from larger models and inference optimizations like quantization to reduce memory requirements.

At full precision, a 30B model would need over 55 GB of memory. Muse Glimmer uses 4-bit quantization, compressing its weights to under 20 GB, which allows it to run within the memory constraints of typical consumer GPUs (24 GB or 32 GB).

Furthermore, Muse Glimmer incorporates a 'drafter' model based on DFlash. This companion network proposes blocks of tokens simultaneously, which the main model verifies, significantly speeding up text generation compared to traditional token-by-token methods without compromising output quality.

Meta has released Muse Glimmer on Hugging Face, with optimized integrations for llama.cpp, MLX, and ExecuTorch expected to follow. This aims to enable developers to deploy a working agent within minutes of downloading the model.
